title: Twelve known RGB fills mapped to the Brother Embroidery thread chart as PE-DESIGN maps them
description: An SVG of twelve 20 x 20 mm squares with chosen RGB fills (pure red, green, blue, yellow, cyan, magenta, mid grey, tan, blue-grey, pale pink, dark green, orange) imported by PE-DESIGN 11.50 as fill regions; PE-DESIGN picked one Brother Embroidery thread per square: rgb(255, 0, 0) -> 800, rgb(0, 255, 0) -> 513, rgb(0, 0, 255) -> 405, rgb(255, 255, 0) -> 205, rgb(0, 255, 255) -> 019, rgb(255, 0, 255) -> 086, rgb(128, 128, 128) -> 817, rgb(200, 150, 100) -> 348, rgb(50, 100, 150) -> 070, rgb(240, 200, 220) -> 124, rgb(20, 80, 40) -> 415, rgb(255, 128, 0) -> 214. OpenStitch imports the same SVG with import.svg, which gives each fill the nearest Brother chart entry 1-61 as PE-DESIGN does (issue #119: equal-weight squared Euclidean, later entry on ties; issue #136: the chart's 61 entries and their codes); the thread table of its PES is compared with PE-DESIGN's.

evidence.note: compat/reference/pes/thread-match-swatches.pes (PE-DESIGN 11.50, 2026-10-29): thread table in sewing order 800, 513, 405, 205, 019, 086, 817, 348, 070, 124, 415, 214 (the table also holds 519 for the unsewn outline slot); PEC colour indices 5, 14, 2, 13, 32, 25, 39, 35, 4, 57, 38, 11; 8488 stitches

compat/reference/pes/thread-match-swatches.svg is the SVG PE-DESIGN imported for the reference (pe-refs-4, SHA-256 747094e4ff85efaf9ae93f01487ca787df9b219582a20d6cef4775e92d9847ca); its colours are listed in the owner's swatches-12.txt

references.make: Home > Import Patterns > from Vector Image: an SVG with the twelve rect elements (x = 5 + 22 * (i mod 4), y = 10 + 25 * (i div 4), 20 x 20 mm, fill rgb(...) as listed, no stroke). PE-DESIGN imports them as Fill Stitch regions at its defaults; change nothing. Save As PES (default type).

measurements.evidence: PE-DESIGN snaps each imported RGB fill to the Brother Embroidery chart (800, 513, 405, 205, 019, 086, 817, 348, 070, 124, 415, 214 for these twelve); OpenStitch's import.svg does the same, and its PES thread table reads back as the same twelve chart threads
